chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sa'id al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who delegated the affair of his wife to a man, so he said, 'Bear witness that I have delegated the affair of so-and-so to so-and-so.' Is that permissible for the man? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to delegate the authority of divorce to another person?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith validates the legal concept of *Tafwid* (delegation), where a husband explicitly authorizes a third party to execute a divorce. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts, allowing for the transfer of specific rights to ensure procedural clarity and mutual consent.
